content.thinking:
The deployment one minute before onset removed the total_this_month_cents field computation from record_purchase, so the monthly total stopped accumulating entirely—this is exactly the silent-data-corruption pattern where the service stays available and fast but spend totals quietly stop reconciling with actual purchases.

The oldest affected purchase lines up precisely with onset time, confirming the deploy as root cause, but the fix classification should be silent-data-corruption rather than bad-deployment since reverting the code won't repair the totals already written incorrectly—only new corruption going forward stops.

For the subject field, I'm weighing whether to use the specific revision hash or the affected code path as the identifier, since silent data corruption isn't really a toggle with clean from/to states like a feature flag would have. I'll treat the deployment itself as the state transition, using the prior revision hash as from_state and the new one as to_state, since that's the concrete before/after that caused the corruption.

I'm ruling out rollout/version-mismatch as the cause since the logs don't show any mismatched-version errors — just unrelated ClientDisconnected errors on the account page — so this looks cleanly like silent data corruption rather than an in-flight compatibility break. Settling on roughly 0.85 confidence and finalizing the answer.

hypotheses.subject: 26f1d7e2c82ce2abff8f9b6424dc226f4f37fed2
hypotheses.summary: A deploy to io-shop at 2026-09-27T12:27:00Z (revision 26f1d7e2c82ce2abff8f9b6424dc226f4f37fed2) changed record_purchase() to stop maintaining total_this_month_cents as a running total, instead deriving it only 'whenever anybody wants it' - but nothing in the diff shows the read path being updated to derive it, so the stored lifetime/monthly totals on shopper accounts silently diverged from the purchases they're supposed to summarize. The metrics stayed flat (no errors, no latency change) because every request was served correctly - only what was written to the account record was wrong, which is exactly what the spend-integrity reconciliation (running every 7 days) caught 240 times with the oldest bad purchase recorded at 2026-09-27T12:28:00Z, one minute after this deploy landed.

hypotheses.summary: If the removal of the monthly-total field was intentional application logic rather than a bug, the same deploy could instead be read as an ordinary bad-deployment that broke the accounting invariant outright (rather than corrupting data silently) - but the alert's framing (240/240 totals wrong, discovered by a periodic reconciliation, metrics flat throughout) fits silent-data-corruption far better than an active failure mode, so this is offered as a fallback only.
